channel.title: AI News Radar
channel.description: A curated 24-hour radar of AI news: official releases, new models and high-signal discussion.

item.title: BaseTab AI — Turn your new tab into an AI-powered workspace
item.description: The headline promises BaseTab AI will turn your new tab into an AI-powered workspace, but the page itself only displays a CAPTCHA security check, with no product or feature details anywhere. (Product Hunt)

item.title: GitHub Copilot Fusion — GitHub's AI coding agent that picks and combines models
item.description: GitHub Copilot Fusion is an AI coding agent that automatically selects and combines different models, aiming to complete coding tasks through multi-model collaboration rather than relying on a single model. (Product Hunt)

item.title: Orkas-AI/Orkas — Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first AI team for your desktop: a Commander turns your goal into to-dos and coordinates 16 built-in specialist agents plus Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes, with projects, scheduled automations and connectors. Free app for macOS & Windows; built-in models or your own keys.
item.description: Orkas is an MIT-licensed, local-first desktop app for macOS and Windows in which a Commander converts your goal into to-dos and coordinates 16 built-in specialist agents alongside Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes, with projects, scheduled automations, connectors and built-in models or your own keys. (GitHub Trending)

item.title: The AI cost of JavaScript frameworks
item.description: Nolan Lawson uses one Pokémon spec and Opus 5.5 via official MCP or skills to generate JavaScript framework code, then runs sandboxed Lighthouse tests for performance and accessibility, asking whether AI-era framework choices have real benchmarks.

item.title: GPT-5.6 Sol can beat Factorio on peaceful mode
item.description: GPT-5.6 Sol, in Codex at low thinking, completed a peaceful Factorio run in 13.5 game hours and launched a rocket via a Python interface, but late-game repeatedly hauled materials to mask failed production-line connections, unlike GPT-5.5, which didn't use belts.

item.title: The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking: Self-Reported (2025)
item.description: A 2025 self-reported study on generative AI's impact on critical thinking is inaccessible here: the page serves only a CAPTCHA bot-verification screen, with no data or conclusions rendered.

item.title: Do the math: How we took over ChatGPT accounts
item.description: By exploiting ChatGPT share links to bypass its sandbox and content security policy, researchers could take over accounts when victims opened a link, reading unshared private conversations until OpenAI fixed the flaw on October 26, 2026, and rated it P1.

item.title: Malware uses LLMs to rank victims by how much they're worth
item.description: The self-deleting VOLTA infostealer steals credentials, sessions and cryptocurrency wallets, then sends its evidence bundle to OpenRouter, where LLMs rank each victim's assets by monetization value and assess OPSEC.

item.title: AI text watermarking and quality loss
item.description: Anthropic’s conclusion that watermarking does not affect quality relied only on human tests of single responses, not multi-turn conversations, as John Gruber criticized Claude’s watermarking after EU AI Act transparency guidelines took effect.

item.title: Anthropic blocks users for anything touching training larger models
item.description: A user claims rollouts came from a strong open-source model, with Claude only helping submit jobs and run analysis, yet Anthropic tagged them for "training a competitor" and blocked anything touching RFT, SFT or larger-model training.
